record.original_question: Let Ω=B^3 be the unit ball in R^3, let g:∂Ω≈S^2→S^2 be smooth with degree deg g=0, and consider weak harmonic maps u∈H^1_g(Ω;S^2) satisfying Δu_i=u_i|∇u|^2 in Ω and u=g on ∂Ω. Does there always exist at least one solution that is continuous on the closed ball Ω̄?

evidence.quote: Since we will be concerned with the existence of continuous harmonic maps satisfying (4.3), we assume throughout this section that (4.5) deg g = 0. ... Open Problem 4.1 ... Assume that (4.5) holds. Does there exist a continuous harmonic map satisfying (4.1)–(4.3)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit ball with boundary $\partial\Omega = S^2$. Let $g : S^2 \to S^2$ be a smooth map of topological degree $\deg g = 0$. Define the Sobolev space
$$H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^3) : |u(x)| = 1 \text{ a.e. in } \Omega,\ u = g \text{ on } \partial\Omega\}.$$
A map $u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ is called a weak harmonic map (into $S^2$) if it satisfies, in the sense of distributions, the system
$$\Delta u_i = u_i\, |\nabla u|^2 \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad i = 1,2,3,$$
together with the boundary condition $u = g$ on $\partial\Omega$.

Question: For every smooth $g : S^2 \to S^2$ with $\deg g = 0$, does there exist at least one weak harmonic map $u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ that is continuous on the closed ball $\overline{\Omega}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in Brezis's collection of favorite open problems. Even when the boundary degree vanishes (removing the obvious topological obstruction), energy-minimizing harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2 are known to develop singularities in general (Hardt–Lin gap phenomenon), and no general construction of a continuous harmonic extension is known. Recent literature (e.g., on the Lavrentiev gap for harmonic maps into spheres) continues to treat this as open.

status_evidence.title: Some of my favorite open problems — Haïm Brezis
status_evidence.snippet: Assume that (4.5) deg g = 0 holds. Does there exist a continuous harmonic map satisfying (4.1)–(4.3)?
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a continuous harmonic map on the closed ball with degree-zero boundary data is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The Lavrentiev gap phenomenon for harmonic maps into spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Even with no topological obstruction, minimizers of the Dirichlet energy of maps B^3 -> S^2 may have singularities (Hardt–Lin gap).
status_evidence.claim: There is a known gap phenomenon obstructing continuous minimizers, supporting that the existence question remains open.
